Title: Ex-CFO grilled for third day over RM370mil plantation deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today recorded for a third consecutive day the statement of a former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body-owned company over alleged abuse of power involving the RM370 million acquisition of shares in two plantation companies.
The statement-taking session at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya lasted more than seven hours.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the former senior executive arrived at the headquarters about 10am.

Title: Brazil hits new diplomatic lows with US and Argentina
Article:
VISAS are being denied, insults are flying, and ambassadors are caught in the crossfire.
Two months before Brazil's election, diplomatic tensions are flaring between President Lula's leftist administration and the right-wing governments of Argentina and the United States.
"We cannot accept interference," leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said in an interview Wednesday, a day after the United States announced it had revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador.
The Trump administration's decision was "irresponsible and ill-advised," Lula told the Meteoro Brasil news outlet.
Relations between Brasilia and Washington have blown hot and cold for months as Lula and his ideological opposite, Donald Trump, have clashed over tariffs, free speech and Brazil's judiciary.
Meanwhile, Brazil this week recalled its ambassador and downgraded diplomatic ties with Buenos Aires after repeated insults from Argentina's firebrand libertarian president Javier Milei, who said Lula was "a thief" and "corrupt."
"This decision remains in effect as long as Javier Milei's attacks on Brazilian democratic institutions persist," a source at Brazil's foreign ministry said Wednesday on condition of anonymity.
Both Trump and Milei are allies of Brazil's far-right Bolsonaro family.
Former president Jair Bolsonaro, 71, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup when he lost his 2022 re-election bid.
In his place, his eldest son Flavio is running for the presidency in October elections.
Lula, 80, has made national sovereignty a key theme of his campaign for a fourth term in office.
"Brazil is not only prepared but will also confront anyone from the outside who seeks to interfere in our electoral process," he said Wednesday.
Washington said it revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador because Brasilia had not yet approved its appointment of Daniel Perez, a prominent Florida Republican, as its ambassador to Brazil.
Lula said that with elections looming, he was not receiving new ambassadors from any country, and blamed Washington for lagging in appointing someone.
"The United States doesn't attach importance to the embassy in Brazil. Trump has been in office for a year and a half, yet he hasn't sent an ambassador here.
"So, they try to send one and think we are obligated to accommodate them on the date they want?" he said.
"That isn't right, nor is it feasible. We want to be treated with respect."
Lula also said Brazil was right to deny visas to two US officials last month, who Washington said were coming to discuss "election integrity" among other things.
Brazil's denial of the visas came after Flavio Bolsonaro renewed debunked claims made by his father that the country's electronic voting system was insecure.
Lula said they were coming to "meddle in, monitor, and investigate Brazil's voting machines."
"I doubt their country has an electoral system more honest than ours," he said.
The latest spat with the US comes just weeks after steep new tariffs came into effect, with Washington accusing the Latin American giant of unfair trade practices.
Tensions with Argentina increased after Milei attended an event launching Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential bid in July, and launched veiled insults at Lula and a Supreme Court justice.
Milei doubled down in an interview broadcast Sunday on Argentine television.
Lula is "a thief, he's corrupt, he's been convicted of theft and corruption, he's been in prison, so it's true that we can call him a convict," Milei said.
Lula, who was previously president from 2003-2010, spent 580 days in jail beginning in April 2018 after being convicted in the sprawling Operation Car Wash anti-corruption probe.
He was freed after his conviction was overturned on procedural grounds, with the presiding judge also later ruled to have been biased.
Lula returned to the presidency in 2023.
* The article is from AFP

Title: Malaysia launches anti-dumping probe, reviews steel import duties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has launched an anti-dumping investigation into certain coated steel imports from China, Chinese Taipei and Vietnam, alongside an expiry review of existing duties on prepainted steel coil imports from China and Vietnam.
The actions follow petitions from local steel manufacturers, who claimed unfairly priced imports continue to harm Malaysia's domestic steel industry, the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said.
One petitioner, NS Bluescope Malaysia Sdn Bhd, sought an investigation into imports of flat-rolled alloy and non-alloy steel products plated or coated with aluminium and zinc from China, Chinese Taipei and Vietnam.
The company alleged the products were exported to Malaysia at prices significantly below their domestic selling prices in the exporting countries, constituting dumping.
It also claimed the volume of dumped imports had increased, causing material injury to the domestic industry.
After assessing the evidence on dumping, injury and the causal link, Miti initiated the investigation under the Countervailing and Anti-Dumping Duties Act 1993 and its accompanying regulations.
The injury assessment covers the period from Jan 1, 2023, to Dec 31, 2025, while the investigation period runs from Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2025.
A preliminary determination will be made within 120 days of the investigation's initiation. If the findings are affirmative, the government may impose provisional anti-dumping duties to prevent further injury to local producers.
Separately, Miti has begun an expiry review of existing anti-dumping duties on imports of prepainted, painted or colour-coated steel coils from China and Vietnam.
The review follows a request by CSC Steel Sdn Bhd, which argued that allowing the current duties to lapse would likely result in continued or recurring dumping and injury to the domestic industry.
Miti said it had assessed the information submitted and decided to initiate the review under the Countervailing and Anti-Dumping Duties Act 1993.
The review covers imports from Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2025, with a final determination to be completed within 180 days from the date of initiation.
For both proceedings, interested parties must submit written representations, questionnaire responses and supporting evidence electronically through the Trade Remedies Investigation Management System by Aug 17, 2026.
Miti said it may base its preliminary or final determinations on the available facts if interested parties fail to provide the required information within the stipulated deadline.

Title: AWC lands third data centre plumbing job in 12 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AWC Bhd has secured a RM23.1 million subcontract for plumbing, silo tank and internal sanitary works at a data centre project, marking its engineering division's third data centre contract in the past 12 months.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the engineering services group said its wholly owned subsidiary, Qudotech Sdn Bhd, accepted a letter of acceptance from a joint venture contractor for the works.
The contract is scheduled for completion by June 2027 and is expected to contribute to the group's earnings for the financial year ending June 30, 2027, until its completion.
Group chief executive officer and president Datuk Ahmad Kabeer Mohamed Nagoor said the latest award reflected customers' confidence in AWC's ability to deliver specialised works for data centre projects.
He said securing three data centre contracts over the past year demonstrated that the segment had become a consistent and growing source of work for the engineering division.
"As demand for data centre infrastructure continues to accelerate, we are increasingly recognised as a trusted partner for complex, mission-critical projects of this nature. We intend to build on this momentum to establish a deeper and more enduring presence in the sector," he said.
Ahmad Kabeer added that AWC would remain focused on executing its healthy order book, which stood at RM865 million as at end-March 2026, excluding the latest contract.
He said projects secured in the previous financial year had started contributing to earnings and were expected to gain further traction as execution progressed.
Headquartered in Subang Jaya, AWC operates four core businesses comprising facilities management, environment, engineering and rail.
Its engineering division specialises in plumbing, building management systems, and heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems.

Title: Foreign investors return to Malaysian equities in July with RM301mil net inflows
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors returned to Malaysian equities in July with RM300.9 million in net inflows, ending two consecutive months of selling.
Buying interest centred on financial services, transportation and logistics, and utilities sectors, according to MBSB Research's latest weekly fund flow report.
Financial services attracted the largest foreign inflows at RM1.11 billion, followed by transportation and logistics at RM367.2 million and utilities at RM305.6 million,
MBSB Research head of research Imran Yassin Yusof said the trading activity suggested investors were favouring sectors with clearer earnings visibility and more defensive characteristics amid a mixed economic outlook.
"Even so, one month of inflows does not establish a durable trend. Elevated producer prices, softer leading indicators and uncertainty over global interest rates could continue to shape investor appetite in the coming months," he said in a statement.
The return of foreign buying was selective, with industrial products and services recording RM759.7 million in net outflows, while technology saw RM484.9 million in foreign selling. Consumer products and services also registered RM212.8 million in outflows.
The buying momentum continued into the final week of July, with foreign institutions recording RM11.1 million in net purchases.
Transportation and logistics led weekly inflows with RM107.4 million, followed by financial services at RM216.5 million and healthcare at RM148 million.
The July inflows came against a mixed economic backdrop, with Malaysia's producer price inflation accelerating to 9.2 per cent year-on-year in June, the strongest annual increase since June 2022, driven largely by supply chain disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's Leading Index declined 0.5 per cent month-on-month in May, with annual growth moderating to 0.8 per cent, pointing to a softer near-term economic outlook, MBSB Research said.
Global monetary conditions also remained uncertain, with the United States Federal Reserve, Bank of England and Bank of Japan keeping their policy rates unchanged in July, although some policymakers continued to flag inflation risks.
Regionally, foreign investors remained cautious, recording US$1.19 billion in net outflows across eight Asian markets tracked by MBSB Research for the sixth consecutive week.
Malaysia was among the markets that attracted foreign inflows, alongside India, South Korea, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines.
MBSB Research said the renewed interest in transportation and logistics, and utilities reflected investor preference for industries linked to trade, mobility, energy and industrial development.
The report noted that while sector classifications do not directly correspond to individual financing programmes, the flow patterns provided an indication of areas where foreign investors were finding relative confidence within the Malaysian market.
MBSB Research said the return of foreign buying was encouraging but should be monitored over a longer period before being viewed as a sustained reversal.
"The July data suggest that foreign investors are again examining selected areas of the Malaysian market.
"Whether that interest develops into a more durable trend will depend on earnings delivery, economic conditions and the ability of strategic industries to convert capital interest into productive investment and business growth," it said.

Title: Na'imah wins bid to quash RM313.8mil tax demand
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Toh Puan Na'imah Abdul Khalid has succeeded in her legal challenge to set aside the Inland Revenue Board's (IRB) demand for RM313.8 million in additional tax.
High Court judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad allowed Na'imah's judicial review application, ruling that the IRB director-general's decision to impose additional tax for the 2018 year of assessment was tainted by illegality and irrationality.
The judge said the assessment was based on three foreign properties that had been acquired decades earlier in the 1990s.
The court made no order as to costs.
After the proceedings, Na'imah's lawyer Datuk S. Saravana Kumar said his client felt vindicated.
"She has consistently maintained that she has been a responsible and compliant taxpayer, and the court's decision affirms her position.
"More broadly, this judgment underscores the judiciary's role as an independent safeguard against the improper exercise of public power," he said.

Title: Pakistan restricts international media reporting outside main cities
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan's government has instructed international media to register journalists and seek permission for any reporting outside the country's three main cities, sparking concern from rights and media groups over a threat to press freedom.
The information ministry sent a statement on Monday to an international media message group on the requirement to seek permission for reporting outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi.
Written guidelines published by the ministry stated all journalists working for international media, including freelance reporters, should register with the government's external media wing.
Organisations would then need to seek Non Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the government for reporting outside the three cities.
It was not clear how widely the guidelines would be enforced or if penalties would apply for non-compliance.
Local media and rights groups called for the requirements to be withdrawn.
They said the rules would curb reporting and freedom of information in the country of 250 million – the world's fifth-most populous nation where many major security, environmental and human rights events unfold outside the three main urban centres.
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan "is deeply concerned by the government's new Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines 2026, which, rather than facilitating journalism, will invariably institutionalise bureaucratic control over news gathering and risk deterring independent reporting on matters of public interest," it said in a statement on Wednesday.
"This is the latest in a growing pattern of restrictions on media freedom in Pakistan," the organisation added, warning that "the space for journalism continues to shrink."
Pakistan is ranked 153 out of 180 nations for press freedom in a Reporters Without Borders index.
Foreign media workers already have to request NOCs for reporting outside the main cities, which could take weeks to obtain, limiting their ability to cover urgent news from the ground.
International media organisations often rely on Pakistani nationals who are based across the country and carry out much of their written and visual coverage of the South Asian nation.
Under the new guidelines, the local journalists would also require an NOC before covering a story.
Pakistan's foreign ministry spokesman on Thursday referred journalists to the information ministry in response to questions on the rules.
The information minister and the ministry's external media wing did not immediately respond to AFP's request for comment.
The instructions come in the wake of protests and a local election in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, during which rights groups decried press restrictions.
The information minister and the ministry's external media wing did not immediately respond to AFP's question on whether the situation in the Himalayan region had prompted the new guidelines.
The Committee to Protect Journalists, an international media advocacy group, posted on X on Monday that it was monitoring "deteriorating press freedom conditions in Pakistan-administered Kashmir amid ongoing protests" and called on authorities to restore access to information and allow independent reporting.
Protests by the Joint Awami Action Committee group demanding electoral reform, and ensuing deadly clashes with law enforcement have been regularly reported on by international media in recent months.
Pakistan's information ministry issued a statement on X on Monday criticising Al Jazeera for the broadcaster's reporting on the polls from the regional capital Muzaffarabad.
The ministry accused the broadcaster of "yellow journalism" and "selective reporting" that corresponds to "the agenda of external actors with vested interests who are attempting to delegitimise this electoral exercise."
Pakistan and neighbouring India both claim Muslim-majority Kashmir in full and have fought several wars over control of the region, which has been divided between the two countries since their independence from British rule in 1947.

Title: Afghan man given life sentence for deadly Munich car-ramming
Article:
MUNICH: A German court on Thursday handed a life jail term to an Afghan man for a car-ramming attack in Munich last year which killed a two-year-old girl and her mother and left dozens injured.
The Munich court ruled that the crime carried "particular gravity", a designation that will make it much harder for the 25-year-old man, named only as Farhad N., to ever win release from prison.
The attack was one of several committed by foreign nationals in the run-up to last year's general election that inflamed debate on immigration and security.
As well as two counts of murder, Farhad N. initially faced 44 counts of attempted murder, but half of these were later replaced by counts of bodily harm, 19 of them serious.
The attack took place as the city prepared to host the Munich Security Conference, a major gathering of high-level figures from the worlds of politics and defence.
A Mini Cooper that was driven into the street rally hurled a 37-year-old woman and her young daughter through the air for 10 metres.
They sustained severe head injuries, of which they died several days later.
An eyewitness quoted by the prosecution described people "being flung left and right, like a bowling alley".

Title: Organisational transformation begins with people, not KPIs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Winning employees' trust and sense of purpose is the first step towards organisational transformation, says former Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) Group Chief Human Capital Officer Datuk Dr Mohd Khalis Abdul Rahim.
Drawing from his experience in leading transformation efforts, he said many initiatives failed because organisations focused on restructuring, processes and performance targets before rebuilding employees' emotional connection with the workplace.
He said organisations must first restore employees' sense of meaning, purpose and pride, especially when financial resources are limited and monetary incentives are not possible.
"You are trying to motivate an organisation to move from a state of slumber to becoming high-performing in a short period without money to incentivise people. What can you give them? You can give them care and pride.
"Tell them we are in this together. We sink and swim together. Give them back meaning, purpose and pride. Without these, they will not buy into the transformation," he said during the Closing Wisdom Exchange session at the 2nd Wisdom Malaysia Conference 2026 here today.
Khalis said organisations should only embark on transformation plans and business recovery strategies after gaining employees' trust and commitment.
He also stressed the importance of consistent communication between leaders and employees, rather than relying solely on formal appraisal sessions.
Transformation leaders, he added, should not depend entirely on consultant-driven frameworks but must understand workplace realities through direct engagement with employees.
The conference, organised by Kerjaya One PLT, brings together current and former industry leaders to share insights on leadership, decision-making and transformation strategies.

Title: Southern Score Builders wins RM146.5mil data centre subcontract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd's unit SJEE Engineering Sdn Bhd has clinched a RM146.5 million subcontract for electrical works at a data centre project.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the company said SJEE was awarded the job by a local construction company to undertake the project's Electrical Package 3 Works (Medium Voltage).
The project commenced on July 27 and is scheduled for completion by Jan 15, 2028.
The company expects the project to contribute to its net assets and earnings per share from the financial year ending June 30, 2027, until completion.
Southern Score Builders has secured four data centre-related contracts worth a combined RM383.05 million so far this year.

Title: MGB completes structural milestone for RM437mil Johor high-rise project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MGB Bhd has completed the topping-out ceremony for Pangsapuri Saujana Indah in Molek, Johor Bahru, marking the completion of the project's main structural works and bringing the developer closer to delivering its first high-rise development in Johor.
The project, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM437 million, comprises two 37-storey residential towers offering 988 units. Tower A features 393 units, while Tower B comprises 595 units, with built-up areas ranging from 590 sq ft to 863 sq ft.
Pangsapuri Saujana Indah is MGB's first high-rise project in Johor and its inaugural development in Johor Bahru, expanding the group's presence beyond its existing markets.
Designed for modern urban living, the development offers a range of lifestyle and community facilities, including a swimming pool, children's playground, multipurpose hall, surau, barbecue area, fitness zone and gymnasium.
The development also features an outdoor recreational park equipped with a running track, aimed at promoting healthier lifestyles and community interaction among residents.
MGB group executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Lim Hock San said the topping-out milestone reflects the commitment and collaboration between the project team, consultants, contractors, suppliers and business partners.
"The completion of the main structural works is a significant achievement and brings us closer to delivering the homes that we have promised to our purchasers. It reflects the dedication, coordination and professionalism of our project team, consultants, contractors, suppliers and business partners," he said.
Since its launch in 2023, Pangsapuri Saujana Indah has received a strong market response, with all 988 units taken up.
Lim said the full take-up demonstrates buyers' confidence in the development's strategic location, practical layouts, comprehensive facilities and value proposition.
He added that MGB remains focused on maintaining high standards of quality, safety and workmanship as the project progresses towards final completion.
"We are committed to ensuring that the remaining works are carried out efficiently and responsibly, with the objective of achieving a smooth and timely completion for homeowners," he said.

Title: Rocky's death highlights need for humane stray animal management - activist
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The death of a dog named Rocky in Klang has highlighted the need to review existing procedures for managing stray animals to ensure enforcement operations are carried out more humanely and systematically.
Community activist Michael Tay said current standard operating procedures (SOPs) may not have fully addressed public sensitivities, concerns of surrounding residents and animal welfare considerations during enforcement operations.
He said every stray animal operation must be conducted without cruelty as animals were living creatures deserving of ethical treatment.
"As humans with reasoning abilities, we have a moral responsibility to ensure every capture operation is carried out ethically and without unnecessary suffering.
"This case should serve as a lesson to establish more organised, transparent and compassionate guidelines for animal control," he said.
He said a suitable step that could be considered is to keep members of the public away from the area where enforcement action is being carried out.
"This can prevent panic, reduce risks and avoid situations that could endanger both people and animals.
"It will also allow enforcement personnel to carry out their duties in a more controlled environment," he said.
He added that human-animal conflicts should not be linked to racial sentiments, but instead viewed as issues involving management effectiveness and SOP implementation.
"As Malaysians, we should respect all communities. Incidents like this should be examined based on weaknesses in management or gaps in existing procedures.
"We should not allow emotions to take over when dealing with viral issues. Instead, we must look at what improvements are needed to prevent a recurrence," he said.
Earlier, Klang Royal City Council (MBDK)
denied any breach of SOPs
during the stray dog capture operation at Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Klang.
MBDK mayor Datuk Abd Hamid Hussain said the incident occurred after a resident claiming to be the dog's owner attempted to intervene and disrupted the operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Customs Dept strengthens response to social media crises with digital training
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Exposure to digital narrative simulations is expected to enhance the ability of Customs Department personnel to manage issues and crises on social media more effectively.
Royal Malaysian Customs Academy (AKMAL) Sarawak branch director Deswita Santari Abdul Khalik said it formed part of a strategic and digital media management course held in Kuching, Sarawak, from Aug 3 to 6.
"We already have existing skills, but this course aims to strengthen the department's capability to act more proactively before an issue escalates into a major crisis.
"Through this course, participants are also exposed to the realities of newsroom operations and the role enforcement agencies must play in delivering timely information to the public," she said in a statement today.
The course involved more than 30 personnel of various ranks from the Customs Department headquarters and branches nationwide.
Deswita said participants were also trained in the proper use of digital tools including InVID WeVerify, Google Reverse Image Search, X Advanced Search, Google Trends and Boardreader.
She said participants were guided through practical sessions on producing digital media content such as rapid response statements, media releases, social media writing, infographic design and effective press conference management.
The four-day workshop was conducted by experts from the Faculty of Communication and Media Studies at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM), who served as trainers and speakers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US requests Filipino pastor's extradition on sex charges
Article:
MANILA: The United States has formally requested the extradition of a Filipino pastor wanted on sex-trafficking charges, the Philippines' ambassador to Washington said on Thursday.
Apollo Quiboloy, a self-proclaimed "Appointed Son of God" and ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in the Philippines in 2024 on human-trafficking charges.
He faces life in prison if found guilty in the case, which accuses him of using women and child sect members to sell goods and raise funds for his church.
Quiboloy, who pleaded not guilty shortly after his August 2024 arrest, has been held in a Manila jail ever since.
A US grand jury had indicted Quiboloy three years earlier for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children, and bulk cash smuggling.
The 2021 US indictment alleges girls and women between the ages of 12 and 25 were recruited as personal assistants for Quiboloy to prepare his meals, clean his residence, give him massages, and have sex with him.
On Thursday, Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez told AFP the United States had formally asked for the pastor to be handed over.
"The formal request has been transmitted to the Dept of Justice," he said via text message, without providing further detail.
The US Embassy and the Philippine Department of Justice did not reply immediately to requests for comment.
Quiboloy was allowed to run for Senate in the country's 2025 midterm elections despite his incarceration and garnered 5,667,438 votes.
Police said following his arrest that Quiboloy's alleged victims were told they were having sex with the "Spirit of God" and were threatened not to tell anyone on pain of being hunted down by "angels of death."
Quiboloy's Kingdom of Jesus Christ church said at the time that members had "freedom of choice" and thus "anything that happens to you... is your own voluntary will or choice."
The powerful sect claims millions of followers in the mainly Catholic Asian nation and owns a television network.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos said in 2024 that the government was not yet looking to extradite Quiboloy because it was "focusing on the cases filed in the Philippines."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia expands KL20 2026 focus to eight sectors to accelerate startup growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will broaden the focus of KL20 2026 from four to eight key sectors as part of efforts to strengthen the startup ecosystem and accelerate the development of higher-value, technology-driven economic activities.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said KL20 2026 would continue to prioritise four existing sectors, energy and green technology, agricultural technology, manufacturing and automation, and Islamic finance, while introducing four new areas.
"Four additional areas have been added, namely the creative economy, digital economy, digital gaming and the third sector, in line with efforts under the 13th Malaysia Plan to increase economic complexity," he said in his keynote address of the KL20 2026 pre-launch today.
He said KL20 must involve the entire ecosystem including government agencies, investors, technology developers, startups, talent institutions and industry players.
KL20 2026 will adopt a more structured, targeted and outcome-oriented approach to strengthen the startup ecosystem and attract high-quality investments.
Launched in 2024, KL20 aims to position Malaysia as a strategic startup hub in Asia and place the country among the world's top 20 ecosystems by 2030.
KL20 2026 will be held under "Activating Malaysia's Tech Arsenal and Open Ecosystem Focus Mission", connecting technology with markets, talent with opportunities and capital with high-potential companies.
Akmal said Malaysia must move beyond being a market where technology is sold and become a country where technology is developed, improved and commercialised.
"Competition is no longer based solely on the resources we have or the strength of our raw materials, but on mastery of technology, data, design, intellectual property, capital and market access," he said.
KL20 2026 will be held across Penang, Johor and Kuala Lumpur, leveraging each location's industrial strengths while connecting regional ecosystems to the national agenda.
Strategic collaborators include Khazanah Nasional Bhd, the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) Northern Corridor Implementation Authority and Iskandar Regional Development Authority.
KL20 Penang, scheduled for Sept 24 at Penang Waterfront Convention Centre, will focus on semiconductors and electrical and electronics (E&E) under "Silicon Surge".
KL20 Johor will follow on Sept 29 at Iskandar Malaysia Studios, focusing on the creative economy and digital gaming under "Creative Reimagined".
"Johor's strategic position and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone could help develop regional networks in gaming, animation, visual effects, digital content and creative technology," said Akmal.
The KL20 2026 main event will return to Kuala Lumpur on Nov 5, bringing together startups, investors, policymakers and industry players across all eight focus areas.
The three-location approach will enable deeper discussions and more targeted engagement instead of concentrating the programme within a single large event.
Akmal said KL20 2026 would pursue four outcomes: measurable impact, stronger capital mobilisation, stronger state ecosystem links and smoother startup growth towards market listing.
"KL20 is an invitation to participate, not merely to observe. We want companies to bring real industrial problems, provide testing environments, open commercial pathways and identify technologies that can be deployed at scale.
"This time, we need to be more targeted. That is why we are moving KL20 to three different locations: Penang, Johor and Kuala Lumpur," he said.
He said KL20 2026 would prioritise building a functioning ecosystem rather than setting headline investment targets, with concrete commitments expected from targeted sectors.
Malaysia's economic performance provided a strong foundation with preliminary second-quarter growth estimated at 5.8 per cent and first-half growth at 5.6 per cent.
Exports rose 27.5 per cent to RM971.6 billion between Jan and June 2026, while Malaysia ranked 15th among 70 economies in the 2026 IMD World Competitiveness ranking.
Akmal said the government would provide policy, infrastructure and facilitation, while commercial validation would depend on companies testing, adopting and scaling solutions.
He said Malaysia had progressed in strengthening its startup ecosystem, but structural issues involving funding, policies, programmes and inter-agency processes remained.
"The platform is already there, but the feedback has not been sufficient. We need to find ways to streamline it better and overcome complexities that prevent startups from focusing on their core strengths," he said.
Akmal said the government was engaging agencies, industry players, technology companies and investors to assess existing initiatives and improve the ecosystem.
He added that Malaysia should approach regional startup development through collaboration rather than treating competition for investment and talent as a zero-sum game.
"We are not looking at this as a zero-sum game. It is more about how we can collaborate further and benefit from each other.
"We have the potential, but that potential has not been fully unleashed. What we want is to create a better ecosystem and leverage our existing strengths to uplift the startup scene," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Actress, company directors among 17 charged over Perkeso claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seventeen people, including company directors and an actress, pleaded not guilty today to charges involving alleged false claims under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme.
The accused, comprising nine men and eight women, were charged separately at Sessions Courts in Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Penang and Sabah over offences allegedly committed in 2024.
In Kuala Lumpur, actress Farah Wahida Zainuddin, 44, and Mohd Nizam Jamaluddin, 45, faced four charges each before Judge Suzana Hussin, while Lim Sue Peng, 54, and Lim Sian Tze, 54, faced five and eight charges respectively before Judge Rosli Ahmad.
Farah Wahida, as director of Focal Reality Entertainment Sdn Bhd, was accused of submitting false employee verification forms to support Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims in March last year, while Mohd Nizam was charged with abetting her.
Sue Peng, director of Zfinity, and Sian Tze, owner of LST Concept Marketing, faced similar charges allegedly committed between April and October 2024.
The four were granted bail ranging from RM6,000 to RM48,000, ordered to report monthly to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), surrender their passports and return to court on various dates in September and October.
In Perak, four business owners faced 29 charges at the Ipoh Sessions Court, while four others in Penang were charged with 30 offences at the George Town Sessions Court.
In Sabah, five people, including four company owners, were charged with nine offences at the Kota Kinabalu Sessions Court.
All charges were framed under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009 and punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the value of the false particulars or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jalan Ampang crash: Prosecution challenges bid to quash murder charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The prosecution has raised a preliminary objection to a college student's application to strike out two murder charges over a road crash that killed a married couple on Jalan Ampang near Great Eastern Mall on May 2.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry said the objection was filed yesterday on grounds that the defence application was procedurally defective and did not comply with the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.
He told reporters this after the case was mentioned before High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin, with defence lawyer S. Selvam representing Danish Raman Kamar Kumaresan, 24.
Selvam informed the court that the defence had filed a notice of motion seeking to strike out the charges, but requested another date to respond to the prosecution's objection.
Aslam fixed Aug 17 to hear the application.
In his application, Danish Raman argued that the public prosecutor's decision to charge him under Section 302 of the Penal Code was mala fide, unreasonable and unconstitutional, claiming it violated Articles 5 and 8 of the Federal Constitution.
He contended that applying the murder provision to a road accident without any intention to kill was contrary to fundamental criminal law principles.
Danish Raman was charged on May 15 with the murder of A. Doraisingam, 61, and his wife, A. Menagah, 56, who died after their Honda Wave Alpha motorcycle was allegedly hit from behind by a Toyota Vios on Jalan Ampang at 5.30am on May 2.
The charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, with not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction.

Title: Court upholds conviction, spares man from gallows in daughter's murder
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A former soldier escaped the gallows after the Federal Court, in a 2-1 majority decision, commuted his death sentence to 40 years' imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane for the murder of his nine-year-old daughter eight years ago.
A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Nordin Hassan, Datuk Seri Vazeer Alam Mydin Meera, and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali upheld the conviction of Mohammad Abdullah Mohamed, 44, under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Delivering the majority decision, Justice Nordin said the court found no miscarriage of justice in the earlier rulings.
"The court finds no miscarriage of justice in the earlier court decision convicting the appellant. Therefore, the conviction under Section 302 of the Penal Code is upheld," he said.
On sentencing, Justice Nordin disclosed that he dissented from the majority, maintaining that the death penalty should have remained.
However, Justices Vazeer Alam and Nazlan ruled that the death sentence should be substituted with 40 years' imprisonment from the date of arrest on Jan 31, 2018, and 12 strokes of the cane.
"You are fortunate that the majority of the panel agreed to substitute the death penalty with a prison sentence," Justice Nordin told the appellant.
Abdullah was charged on Feb 12, 2018, with killing his 9-year-old daughter,
Nur Aina Nabihah
, on Jan 31 the same year.
On Aug 22, 2023, the Seremban High Court sentenced Abdullah to death after finding him guilty of murdering Nur Aina Nabihah at a house in Taman Vista Jaya, Lukut, Port Dickson, between 8.30pm and 11.30pm on Jan 31, 2018.
The Court of Appeal upheld both the conviction and the death sentence on June 26, 2025.
Earlier, lawyer  Afifuddin Ahmad Hafifi, representing Mohammad Abdullah, argued that the conviction was unsafe because the trial court had relied on the testimony of the prosecution's 18th witness (SP18), the victim's elder brother, without first conducting a competency assessment.
He submitted that intelligence alone was insufficient to establish a witness's competence to testify under oath and urged the court to give his client a second chance.
Afifuddin also told the court that the appellant had taken the victim to hospital for treatment.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin countered that SP18, who was 15 when he testified, clearly understood the questions posed during the trial and was a competent witness.
He said SP18 testified that he and the victim were punished by their father for failing to perform their prayers, with both children ordered to do 500 push-ups and sit-ups.
"When the victim could no longer continue, the accused allegedly kicked and stomped on her abdomen, causing her pancreas to rupture. She also suffered broken ribs, signs of strangulation on her neck, blunt force trauma to the head, and a total of 23 external injuries.
Wan Shaharuddin argued that the brutality of the abuse and the appellant's lack of remorse meant he did not deserve a second chance, adding that the public expected the death penalty in such circumstances.
Speaking to reporters after the proceedings, Wan Shaharuddin said the prosecution accepted the Federal Court's decision.
"I am grateful the court imposed a 40-year prison sentence. While serving that sentence, he must reflect on what he did to his child. That is worse than the death penalty," he said.

Title: Ministry invites stakeholder feedback to strengthen use, purchase of local products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government invites all stakeholders to submit proposals and feedback to ensure that the policies and strategies to enhance the use and purchase of local products are truly aligned with the industry's needs.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said that suggestions and views can be channelled to the ministry or relevant agencies, and they will be presented to the Cabinet Committee to empower the use and purchase of local products, which is expected to hold its first meeting soon.
He said that the step is important to coordinate the efforts of various ministries and agencies in an integrated manner and no longer operate in silos.
"This step is important so that we can drive and formulate directions, strategies, and approaches that also encompass ideas, suggestions, and views from stakeholders," he said to reporters after attending the Fashion Forward Batik segment at the Kuala Lumpur Fashion Week (KLFW) 2026 here today.
The Cabinet Committee to empower the use and purchase of local products, established in July, is chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, with the ministry acting as the secretariat.
The committee aims to coordinate the efforts of various ministries and agencies so that they no longer operate in silos, thereby reducing dependence on imported products, increasing the contribution of local products to the country's economic growth, and assisting local entrepreneurs.
"In addition to strengthening local products, another issue that arises is the concerns and worries of local entrepreneurs due to the influx and also the flooding of foreign products from outside, including those sold through online platforms," he said.
He said the committee also involves the Economy Ministry,  of Investment Trade and Industry Ministry (MITI); Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives  Ministry, Finance Ministry, and various related agencies.
Regarding KLFW, Armizan said that the strategic collaboration between his ministry and KLFW is part of the implementation of the Jom Beli Produk Malaysia (Jom Malaysia) movement to empower local products through a collaborative approach with industry players.
The event is said to have the potential to serve as an important platform for expanding access to the batik market and local products to the international level, based on a media value record of USD32 million achieved by the event's organisation last year.
That achievement proves that KLFW has a wide influence and reach in the fashion industry, thereby strengthening the branding of local products in the global market.
He also said that efforts to empower the cultural and creative industries are also in line with the development of the sector, which contributed RM130.7 billion or 6.8 per cent to the gross domestic product (GDP) based on the 2024 Cultural and Creative Satellite Account Report.

Title: India youth protests highlight mistrust in 'lapdog' media
Article:
JOURNALISTS covering last month's youth-led protests in India became targets of public anger and attacks over their perceived support for the government, exposing a deepening crisis of trust in traditional broadcasters.
In rallies across the country spearheaded by the online Cockroach Janta Party movement, protest signs branded TV channels as "India's worst enemies", and activists criticised "lapdog" media said to be aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration.
The hostility underscored a widening gulf between legacy networks and a growing ecosystem of independent digital outlets that many young Indians increasingly turn to for news.
At New Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site, many students said they relied on social media and independent platforms.
"It is disheartening to see news channels," said Sukhjeet Narula, 28, a software professional.
"They brand every protest anti-national."
The immediate backlash saw protesters target TV journalists.
Dev Kotak, a reporter with prominent English-language network Times Now, said a crowd in New Delhi threw water at him, but that quickly escalated into slaps and kicks.
"There was anger simmering around me and I was scared for my life," the 36-year-old told AFP.
Videos of an exhausted Kotak running behind security personnel as protesters pursue him spread on social media.
Three of his colleagues were also harassed.
In other footage verified by AFP, a reporter with Zee TV was heckled while broadcasting live from a protest in Mumbai.
Another video showed a journalist being chased by a crowd in the eastern city of Patna.
The Times Network said they had covered the protests in an "entirely neutral manner" but their journalists were still "assaulted in the most reprehensible manner."
"We may differ in views, but we cannot take the law into our own hands," it said in a statement.
Media observers say the public anger reflected years of eroding confidence.
"Godi media are considered anti-people and anti-opposition," journalist Ravish Kumar told AFP.
The term "godi" – "lap" in Hindi – is used by critics to refer to so-called "lapdog" media accused of abandoning their watchdog role.
[[nid:1505482]]
"They have destroyed their own credibility. Genuine public demands are being termed as conspiracies in order to demonise them," said Kumar.
Rights groups have raised concerns about press freedom since Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in 2014, citing growing hostility towards journalists perceived as critical of the government.
India ranks 157th out of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index, down 17 places from 2013.
Journalists critical of the government have faced criminal cases, arrests and online harassment from supporters of the ruling party.
Opposition politicians have long accused news channels of peddling BJP's agenda, including through polarising coverage of Muslim minorities.
Tensions surrounding the protests became so intense that some TV journalists opted to conceal the name and logo of their organisations.
"They stopped coming with logos on their mics because the youth were targeting them," said Shailendra Singh, 30.
"The mainstream media has completely sold out to the government," added the private sector employee.
Atul Chaurasia, managing editor of the Newslaundry digital platform, argued that traditional newsrooms relied on a "flawed financial model" that depended heavily on advertising revenue from the government.
"The government weaponises advertising, effectively destroying the environment that allows media organisations to operate freely," he told AFP.
Kumar said it was important to distinguish between large TV networks and independent outlets that often face pressure from authorities.
"It is the alternative media and independent journalists who face hostility from the government," he said.
"They are subjected to raids, branded anti-national, or even imprisoned."
The recent outburst of anger, Kumar argued, reflected a broader perception that some TV networks have become "a threat to democracy."
"Godi" media outlets have "become a liability, even for Prime Minister Modi", he said.
* The writers are from AFP

Title: Malaysia, Vietnam deepen defence ties amid regional challenges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Vietnam are set to strengthen defence cooperation through greater collaboration in military training, intelligence sharing, maritime domain awareness and emerging security challenges.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the areas were discussed during his bilateral meeting with Vietnam's Minister of National Defence General Phan Văn Giang during his two-day official visit to the country.
He said Malaysia had proposed enhancing the existing cooperation mechanism through a High-Level Committee to ensure initiatives were better coordinated and implemented.
"Various areas of cooperation were discussed, including bilateral military training, intelligence sharing, maritime domain awareness, submarine rescue operations, artificial intelligence (AI), the defence industry, and efforts to address emerging security challenges such as grey zone activities," he said in a statement.
Khaled said both sides also exchanged views on regional developments, including the South China Sea.
"Malaysia emphasised that peace and stability must continue to be preserved through dialogue, diplomacy and international law, while supporting the finalisation of an effective and meaningful Code of Conduct (COC)," he said.
He said he appreciated Phan's positive response to Malaysia's proposals and his commitment to further strengthen bilateral defence ties.
"I am confident this shared commitment will continue to strengthen Malaysia-Vietnam defence relations while contributing towards peace, stability and prosperity in Asean," he said.

Title: Defence at heart of Malaysia-Canada ties as new pact takes shape
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Canada is seeking to strengthen defence ties with Malaysia as part of its broader commitment to building partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, with a bilateral defence cooperation agreement expected to be signed next year.
Canadian Armed Forces Senior Military Representative-Indo-Pacific (SMR-IP) Lieutenant-General Derek Macaulay said the proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU), which has been under negotiation since 2024, was progressing well.
He said the agreement would serve as a starting point for both countries to explore further opportunities to share knowledge and strengthen defence cooperation.
"There's great anticipation that the defence cooperation agreement would actually be signed in the coming year because I think that allows us, as a start point, to look at other opportunities to share and to learn from one another," he said in an interview with the New Straits Times.
He said the agreement would build on nearly seven decades of Malaysia-Canada ties, with defence serving as a cornerstone of relations since diplomatic ties were established in 1957.
The two countries will mark the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year.
Macaulay is the first senior military officer to helm Canada's newly created SMR-IP position, which focuses on developing reliable and trusted partnerships with countries in the Indo-Pacific.
"The establishment of the SMR-IP position reflected Canada's commitment to having a dedicated three-star military officer focused on strategic engagement with Indo-Pacific partners.
"The creation of this position sends a signal of strength and the fact that we want to strengthen our partnerships," he said.
He said Canada's increased regional focus follows the launch of its Indo-Pacific Strategy, which includes diplomatic, economic and military components.
"We don't want to have a cookie-cutter solution. We want to look at each individual country as its own respectful sovereign nation and see what really fits with them.
"We're looking forward to working with them, not telling them what to do from a Canadian perspective," he said.
On bilateral defence cooperation with Malaysia, Macaulay said the Military Training and Cooperation Programme, established in 1966, have trained more than 750 Malaysian officers in areas including language training, professional military education and women, peace and security (WPS).
"Cooperation had also expanded into areas such as chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear threat mitigation through Exercise Mantis," he said.
On defence industry cooperation, Macaulay said both countries' defence industrial strategies presented opportunities for collaboration, particularly under Canada's 'build, partner, buy' framework.
He said Canada is keen to work with trusted partners such as Malaysia to strengthen both countries' defence industries, while Canadian companies had also shown growing interest in participating in Malaysian defence exhibitions, including the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima).
"We're looking for those trusted partners, those reliable partners, those partners that we've had great relationships with throughout decades," he said.
Macaulay said Canadian companies were already operating in Malaysia and expressed confidence that successful ventures would encourage more Canadian firms to explore opportunities in the country.
He also reaffirmed Canada's commitment to a free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific, with respect for international law, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Asean centrality and dialogue in resolving disputes.
He said Canada viewed Malaysia as an important regional partner and would continue to deepen engagement based on mutual respect, shared interests and the needs identified by both countries.

Title: MPV driver laments wild elephants breaching LPT2 after collision
Article:
CHUKAI: The driver of a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) that collided with a herd of wild elephants at Km274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) here last Tuesday has expressed disappointment over the highway's safety measures, claiming they failed to prevent wild animals from entering the carriageway and endangering motorists.
Victim Abdul Wahid Ismail, 55, from Kampung Pasir Gajah here, said the incident came as a shock as the herd was on the highway and appeared suddenly at night, leaving him with no time to avoid the collision.
He said motorists using the highway face the risk of even more serious accidents if elephants and other wild animals continue to breach the expressway in future.
He therefore supported Works Minister Datuk Seri
Alexander Nanta Linggi
's directive yesterday for the LPT2 concessionaire to immediately repair damaged safety fencing and review long-term measures to enhance motorists' safety following the incident.
"Before a more serious accident claims lives, it is better for immediate action to be taken to repair the safety fencing and strengthen preventive measures to ensure such incidents do not recur," he told reporters at his home in Kampung Pasir Gajah here today.
The lorry driver said he plans to seek compensation from the LPT2 concessionaire over the accident.x
"The accident left my wife, Fauziah Muda, 52, with a fractured right arm, while our vehicle was also badly damaged," he said.
In the 10.20pm incident last Tuesday, the couple sustained injuries after their Toyota Estima MPV crashed into a herd of elephants on the road after the Cheneh toll plaza exit.

Title: Malaysia secures RM791.5mil in Farnborough Airshow deals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia secured RM791.54 million in export sales from its participation at the Farnborough International Airshow (FIA) 2026 in the United Kingdom, reflecting growing global confidence in the country's aerospace capabilities.
The five-day event, held from July 20 to 24, saw the Malaysia Pavilion facilitate 148 business meetings between Malaysian companies and international aerospace stakeholders, according to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade).
The pavilion, coordinated by Matrade in collaboration with the National Aerospace Industry Corp Malaysia (Naico), featured 15 Malaysian exhibitors alongside Invest Selangor Bhd and the Malaysia Aerospace Industry Association (MAIA).
The exhibitors showcased capabilities across key aerospace segments, including aerostructures manufacturing, precision machining, aerospace finishing, electronic design and hardware, manufacturing solutions, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), aviation services and aerospace events.
Matrade chief executive officer Abu Bakar Yusof said the commercial outcomes reaffirmed Malaysia's competitiveness as a trusted aerospace manufacturing and supply chain partner.
He said Malaysia's aerospace industry generated RM32.5 billion in revenue in 2025, with exports contributing RM7.95 billion or 24.5 per cent of total industry revenue.
"As we work towards achieving the Malaysia Aerospace Industry Blueprint (MAIB) 2030 target of RM55.2 billion in industry revenue, expanding high-value exports will remain a key growth driver alongside domestic aerospace manufacturing, MRO, systems integration and engineering services," he said in a statement.
Abu Bakar said FIA 2026 had reinforced global confidence in Malaysian aerospace capabilities, creating opportunities for local companies to secure higher-value programmes, deepen partnerships with global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and strengthen their position in international supply chains.
He added that Matrade would continue enhancing market access opportunities for Malaysian companies, particularly small and medium enterprises, to expand internationally.
Meanwhile, Naico Malaysia chief executive officer Dr Shamsul Kamar Abu Samah said the strong results demonstrated the growing depth, technical readiness and maturity of Malaysia's aerospace ecosystem.
"As global OEMs accelerate production ramp-ups and seek resilient supply chain partners, NAICO Malaysia remains committed to enhancing the capability and technological adoption of local suppliers," he said.
During the exhibition, CTRM Aero Composites Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of CTRM Holdings Sdn Bhd, received the 2026 Asia Best Maturity Award at the Aero Excellence International Best Maturity Awards after achieving the Bronze Maturity Level under the Aero Excellence Industrial Assessment Programme.
The recognition highlighted Malaysia's manufacturing capabilities, operational standards and supply chain resilience, further strengthening confidence among global aerospace players.
Matrade said FIA 2026 also highlighted opportunities for Malaysian companies amid global aerospace growth driven by commercial aircraft and engine commitments, production ramp-ups, next-generation propulsion technologies, sustainable aviation solutions and autonomous defence systems.
The agency added that its Virtual Malaysia Pavilion on the Madani Digital Trade Platform (MDTP) continued generating international interest throughout the exhibition, with participating companies recording hundreds of profile visits and buyer engagements.
The platform provides international buyers with year-round access to Malaysian aerospace capabilities and supports continued business engagement beyond physical exhibitions.
Matrade said it would continue working with industry stakeholders to promote Malaysian aerospace companies in strategic international markets and strengthen Malaysia's position as Southeast Asia's leading aerospace manufacturing, engineering and services hub.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Auditor General blocked from probing Najib's accounts, says Pua [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Auditor General was barred from examining Datuk Seri Najib Razak's bank accounts during its audit of 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), the High Court heard today.
Former Public Accounts Committee (PAC) member Tony Pua said the restriction, coupled with 1MDB's failure to provide key documents, significantly limited the audit's scope.
Testifying in 1MDB's US$5.64 billion civil suit against Najib and seven others, Pua said the Auditor General had to rely solely on 1MDB's audited financial statements and supporting documents provided by the company's external auditors.
He said 1MDB did not provide several crucial documents, including investment agreements and bank statements belonging to its overseas subsidiaries.
"Due to the substantial lack of cooperation from 1MDB, the Auditor General carried out its audit by reviewing only 1MDB's audited financial statements with supporting documents provided by the relevant auditors.
"No investigations or questions were allowed on Najib Razak's accounts," he said.
Pua also referred to the Auditor General's interim report, which was later cited by then second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Husni Hanadzlah, who urged critics to stop making unfounded allegations after the report found no evidence of wrongdoing.
Earlier, judicial commissioner Mohamad Redzuan allowed Najib's lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah's application to remove parts of Pua's witness statement, ruling that they contained personal opinions and hearsay.
The expunged portions included references to media reports on the 1MDB scandal, including articles by Sarawak Report, as well as claims concerning the removal of former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail.
The court noted that Gani had resigned.
The hearing continues.

Title: Pacific islands alarmed by Trump-backed push for deep-sea mining
Article:
SYDNEY: A Pacific island leader says there were "no consultations" before the US announced swathes of nearby ocean could be auctioned for deep-sea mining exploration, telling AFP the industry faced strong opposition among his people.
Commonwealth of Northern Mariana Islands Governor David Apatang said the idea had caused great unease across the tropical island chain of some 40,000 people.
The United States alarmed its tropical island territories earlier this year, detailing plans to carve up parts of the Pacific Ocean for mining exploration.
Mining companies see enormous wealth in mineral deposits scattered across the seabed, but the fledgling industry has for years been held back by environmental concerns.
An expanse of US maritime territory near American Samoa in the South Pacific could be auctioned as soon as November, according to official documents.
Separate tracts of ocean surrounding Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands in the Western Pacific are also under consideration.
"Some concerns include disruption to food security for the people of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, who rely on the ocean resources for their survival," Apatang told AFP.
Washington initially proposed to explore a 140,000 square kilometre (50,000 square mile) block about 200 kilometres east of territory capital Saipan.
But Apatang said he was caught by surprise when the US announced in March that a similar-sized block to Saipan's west could be leased as well.
"There have been no consultations with the people of the Northern Mariana Islands," he said.
Deep-sea mining companies want to scour the ocean's abyssal plains for mineral deposits and polymetallic nodules laden with nickel, copper and cobalt.
US President Donald Trump signed an executive order in 2025 aimed at "unleashing" these seabed resources, stressing the demand in everything from renewable energy to military applications.
Critics fear deep-sea mining will cause irreversible damage, smothering marine life in plumes of waste and disrupting oceanic migrations with the thrum of heavy machinery.
The Mariana Islands, Guam and American Samoa all want at least a temporary ban on deep-sea mining in their territorial waters.
But the US territories – which rely on Washington for funding and defence – have little say on what Washington does outside their five kilometre maritime boundary.
[[nid:1505467]]
Guam passed laws this year banning deep-sea mining vessels from calling at its ports, potentially hampering the industry by cutting off a crucial source of fuel and supplies.
Apatang said the Northern Mariana Islands would "consider following suit."
Plans for deep-sea mining exploration are most advanced for a vast sweep of ocean near American Samoa, a US territory nestled between New Zealand and Hawaii in the South Pacific.
The US Bureau of Ocean Energy Management is proposing to hold an auction in November, selling exploration licenses for a 125,000 square kilometre block.
The area borders the vast Rose Atoll marine sanctuary, where endangered species of Hawksbill turtle thrive on vibrant reefs.
Lawmaker Aumua Amata, who represents American Samoa in the US House of Representatives, said she worried deep-sea mining could disrupt fisheries providing the vast bulk of the territory's export earnings.
"I represent our people and I am confident that a majority of American Samoans are opposed," she told AFP.
The licenses cover preliminary surveys and sampling, with future decisions on commercial exploitation needing further bureau approval.
American Samoa-based environmental advocate Sabrina Suluai-Mahuka said it was impossible to put a "price tag" on the ocean.
"It's not something you think: 'How much money can you make off it?'."
Former US diplomat Emily Wood has been working with the Guam governor's office to better understand the risks of deep-sea mining.
She said leading mining company Impossible Metals had pledged to share one percent of profits with island communities.
"That's nothing at all, compared to the potential damage they might cause," she told AFP.
Impossible Metals did not reply to a request for comment.
The company has previously stated it will not start mining until it is satisfied it is safe.
Pacific island nations are divided on whether deep-sea mining will deliver economic windfalls, or environmental catastrophe.
Nauru and the Cook Islands are among world leaders in seabed mining exploration, while the likes of Samoa, Fiji and Palau have called for a moratorium on the industry.

Title: MyCreative: Grants open to help artists break into global market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians are encouraged to tap available government financial support to expand their reach and elevate the local creative industry, said MyCreative Ventures group chief executive officer Zainol Haqim Zainol Rashid.
"Programmes and funding initiatives like these serve as a platform for those who wish to venture into the creative sector. They should seize these opportunities.
"Under the Creative Content Fund, we offer the Marketability Fund, where artists looking to produce a new album can apply for financial support. This is not restricted to established artists," he said.
MyCreative Ventures is a government investment arm tasked with spurring Malaysia's creative sector through strategic and innovative funding and investment.
Zainol said applications for the Creative Content Fund for the music sector are open until mid-September, adding that local artists invited to perform abroad can also seek financial backing.
"We also have the International Marketing and Promotion Fund. If an artist receives an invitation to perform overseas, they can apply. This is aimed at fostering mobility and enabling us to export our local talent abroad," he said.
Highlighting the success of previous grant recipients who managed to market their products internationally, Zainol said the long-term aim of these funding initiatives is to build a self-sustaining industry.
"We will continue this initiative until our industry players reach a point where they no longer require government assistance," he said.
Zainol was speaking during a working visit to Media Prima Bhd at Balai Berita in Bangsar today.
He led a MyCreative Ventures delegation to strengthen strategic cooperation and explore new collaborative opportunities with Media Prima.
During the visit, the delegation toured Media Prima's radio studios, the New Straits Times Press (NSTP) archives and TV3's Buletin Utama studio.
The visit concluded with a meeting with Media Prima group managing director Datuk Mohd Rafiq Mat Razali.

Title: Aeon Bank integrates MyTentera ID for seamless digital onboarding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aeon Bank has integrated MyTentera ID into its electronic know-your-customer (eKYC) verification process, allowing Malaysian armed forces personnel to complete identity verification seamlessly during digital banking onboarding.
The integration, introduced ahead of Hari Pahlawan, enables eligible armed forces personnel of all ranks with a valid MyTentera ID to download the Aeon Bank application, complete the onboarding process and activate their Savings Account-i anytime and anywhere.
Aeon Bank said the move reinforces its commitment to providing inclusive, convenient and customer-focused digital banking solutions for Malaysians.
Following successful onboarding, customers can access the bank's suite of Shariah-compliant products and services, including Savings Account-i, Aeon Bank x Visa Debit Card-i, Term Deposit-i, Savings Pot, DuitNow QR, Zakat, Takaful, JomPAY, utility bill payments and digital payment services through Aeon Bank's strategic partners and merchant network.
The bank also offers Neko Missions, which it described as Malaysia's first gamified digital banking interactive rewards programme, alongside Neko Sensei, an artificial intelligence-powered personal financial coach.
For eligible deposit-based products under Aeon Bank and Aeon Bank Biz, including Savings Account-i, Savings Pot, Term Deposit-i, Business Current Account-i and Biz Term Deposit-i, deposits are protected up to RM250,000 per depositor.
Aeon Bank is a member of Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM), with deposit protection provided automatically and free of charge.
The digital bank said it will continue strengthening its digital capabilities and developing innovative Shariah-compliant banking solutions to enhance customer experiences while supporting the growth of Islamic banking and Malaysia's digital economy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Syndicates switch to trains to smuggle drugs, say Thai police
Article:
KOTA BARU: Thai police believe drug syndicates from Malaysia and several neighbouring countries have changed their smuggling tactics, including using trains to transport drugs out of Thailand to evade detection by authorities.
Deputy Commissioner of Provincial Police Region 9 Major General Waesamae Saelae said the shift in modus operandi was uncovered following the arrest of 3 Malaysians with 87kg of syabu worth an estimated RM4.3 million on July 31.
He said police believe the change was prompted by intensified enforcement operations against drug trafficking networks by Thai authorities.
"Authorities have stepped up anti-drug operations, including setting up roadblocks and carrying out extensive enforcement activities to track down those involved in drug trafficking.
"In the past, traffickers typically used their own vehicles to transport the drugs.
"Now, they have switched to public transport, including trains, in an attempt to avoid detection," he said when contacted.
Waesamae said police also believe the new tactic is being adopted by syndicates operating from Malaysia and several neighbouring countries as law enforcement agencies continue tightening surveillance along key trafficking routes.
He said the 3 Malaysian suspects had recently been transferred from Hat Yai to a prison in Bangkok, where the case is now being handled by police headquarters.
"The case is still under investigation, and I believe they will be charged in court within 1 or 2 months," he said.
Waesamae said Thai police would continue strengthening intelligence sharing and enforcement efforts to disrupt cross-border drug trafficking networks and bring those responsible to justice.
It was previously reported that 3 Malaysians travelling by train from Bangkok to Hat Yai were
arrested
by Thai police after 87kg of syabu worth about RM4.3 million was found concealed in their luggage.
On Tuesday, Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 3 men were believed to have acted as drug mules.
He said the trio, all from Sarawak, were
arrested
aboard the Bangkok-Narathiwat Express train during security checks on passengers and their belongings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK's Harworth gets US$784mil takeover bid from top investor Peel Holdings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Peel Holdings has offered to buy British land and property regeneration company Harworth Group in a deal valuing the London-listed firm at about £582.9 million (US$784.41 million), the real estate investor said on Thursday.
Peel Holdings, part of British businessman John Whittaker's Peel Group, is the largest shareholder at Harworth with a nearly 30 per cent stake.
Peel Holdings is offering 172.5 pence in cash per Harworth share for the shares it does not already own.
Shares in Harworth were up 21 per cent at 174 pence as of 0708 GMT.
The offer represents a premium of about 20.1 per cent to Harworth's closing share price on August 5.
Peel Holdings said it believes Harworth's assets would be "best owned, managed and developed" under full private ownership.
Harworth owns and manages a portfolio of assets comprising modern industrial and logistics investment properties and land holdings in the North of England and the Midlands.
